correctness.rationale: A projected equatorial polygon is an ellipse-affine regular n-gon with normals at odd angular offsets. All vertices survive exactly when each added opposite apex violates precisely one distinct projected polygon facet. For odd n the nearest positive/negative normal gaps are x and a-x; d=max(x,a-x) is uniform on [a/2,a] with density 2/a, and second closest gap is 2a-d. The Haar vertical absolute direction is independent Uniform[0,1]. Integrating the exact facet window gives 2/a*[2asin(q sin a)-asin(q sin(a/2))-asin(q sin(3a/2))]. A power-series derivative with a single sign change in coefficients proves a unique q in (0,1), including n=3 endpoint case. A uniform t->0 expansion provides the n^-2 limit and optimizer limit. Independent quadrature of the Haar facet-window integral agrees at 18 (n,h) pairs, but the proof is analytic.
